summary: CCC-built 1942 stone-and-wood L-4 lookout in the Bighorns, renamed in 2015 for a ranger who died in the 1937 Blackwater Fire; manned only in high fire seasons.

access.note: Forest Service recreation site; seasons of use depend on the weather

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bighorn National Forest

events.note: James T. Saban died fighting the Blackwater Fire on the Shoshone National Forest; the fire was not at this lookout
Planned summer 1941 completion; the rock work needed a stonemason
Completed by the CCC to standardized USFS plans; the register, nomination, Wikipedia and firelookout.com all give 1942
Paid lookouts until the late 1970s; the period of significance ends in 1979 as day-to-day operation moved to volunteers
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on November 15, 1991
Renamed for James T. Saban by order of the Chief of the Forest Service on April 7, 2015
Listed on the National Register in late 2016; Wikipedia gives November 15, the register says December

corrections.why: 1937 is the year James T. Saban died in the Blackwater Fire. The register, the nomination and firelookout.com all date the CCC completion to 1942, and a 1941 letter shows the lookout still unfinished that summer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1937 build year matches the year Saban died, not the construction. The construction sources give 1942, and a 1941 letter shows the lookout was still being finished that summer. No source read describes an earlier lookout on the site.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict left unresolved: register 9,395 ft (2,864 m, matches the record's 2863.6 m) vs Forest Service 9,477 ft. NRHP listing date: register says December 2016, Wikipedia says November 15, 2016. Footprint: register and Wikipedia give 14 ft square, the nomination gives a 20 ft exterior footprint. The Forest Service page spells the name 'James Torrey Saban'; the register says 'James T.', so the story keeps 'James T.' and does not expand it. Current staffing and access come from the Forest Service page (last updated May 13, 2025), not a site visit. A search snippet about an overnight rental concerned Sheep Mountain, a different lookout, and was not used. The nomination gives no date for the restoration work. No new photos.
